title: Local weights and reality
statement:
Use the coefficient embedding $\iota$, curve and residue cardinalities of [sk-d-real-setup]. For a Weil sheaf $\mathcal F$, given by a representation $\rho$ of
$W(C_0)$ on a finite-dimensional $\Qlb$-vector space $V$,
and a closed point $x$ with local Frobenius $F_x$ of [sk-d-real-weil], use the reverse characteristic polynomial [def-weil-reverse-characteristic-polynomial] to set

$$
P_x(\mathcal F,T)=\det(1-T\rho(F_x)\mid V),\qquad
\wt_{\iota,q_x}(\alpha)=
\frac{2\log|\iota(\alpha)|}{\log q_x}
$$

The formula is for a nonzero local eigenvalue $\alpha$ and the residue cardinality $q_x$ of $x$. Here $|\cdot|$ is complex absolute value [def-weil-complex-absolute-value], and $\log$ is the natural logarithm on positive reals [def-wf-positive-real-logarithm]. A local eigenvalue is a root of the characteristic polynomial [def-weil-characteristic-polynomial] of $\rho(F_x)$ (equivalently, an inverse root of $P_x$); its algebraic multiplicity is its root multiplicity [def-weil-root-multiplicity].
The sheaf is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w\in\mathbf R$ if, at every closed
point $x$, all these weights are $w$, and has weights at most $w$ if all
are $\le w$.
It is $\iota$-real if $\iota P_x(\mathcal F,T)\in\mathbf R[T]$ for every
$x$, equivalently if each complex local eigenvalue multiset is stable
under complex conjugation $z=a+bi\mapsto\overline z=a-bi$, with multiplicities. This condition is imposed on polynomials.
For a constructible Weil sheaf the same definitions are made with the
stalk $\mathcal F_{\bar x}$ and its local geometric Frobenius $F_x$ (the stalk-operator convention of [def-weil-punctual-weights], with the embedding $\iota$ still as fixed here) in place of $V$ and
$\rho(F_x)$.

proof.text: Fix a closed point $x$ and write $F=\rho(F_x)$ and $n=\dim V$. Since $\rho$ is a group representation, $F$ is an automorphism. By [lem-weil-charpoly-monic-degree], $\chi_F$ is monic of degree $n$. Apply [lem-weil-alg-closed-linear-factorization] over the algebraically closed field $\Qlb$ to obtain $\chi_F(U)=\prod_{j=1}^n(U-\alpha_j)$, with the roots repeated according to their algebraic multiplicities. Its constant coefficient is nonzero: [lem-weil-endomorphism-invertible-iff-det-nonzero] gives $\det F\ne0$, and [lem-weil-charpoly-constant-coefficient-det] gives $\det F=(-1)^n\chi_F(0)$. Thus every $\alpha_j$ is nonzero. By [lem-weil-reverse-charpoly-eq-reverse] and the finite-product clause of [lem-weil-polynomial-reflection-multiplicative], reversing these degree-one factors gives $P_x(T)=\prod_{j=1}^n(1-\alpha_jT)$. Its degree is $n$, since its leading coefficient is $\prod_j(-\alpha_j)\ne0$, and $P_x(0)=1$. Clause 3 of [lem-weil-reciprocal-root-factorization] now identifies its reciprocal-root multiset with the $\alpha_j$, including multiplicities. For $n=0$ both products are $1$ and the multisets are empty.

proof.text: The choice of local Frobenius in [sk-d-real-weil] changes $F$ to $AFA^{-1}$ for an invertible $A$. In the basis obtained by applying $A$ to an original basis, the matrix of $AFA^{-1}$ is exactly the original matrix of $F$. The basis-independent determinant construction [def-weil-reverse-characteristic-polynomial] therefore gives the same $P_x$; the same argument for $\det(U-F)$ gives the same characteristic polynomial [def-weil-characteristic-polynomial] and root multiplicities. All the displayed local quantities and predicates are consequently independent of this choice.

proof.text: Apply $\iota$ to the factorization of step 1, obtaining $Q_x(T)=\iota P_x(T)=\prod_j(1-z_jT)$ with $z_j=\iota(\alpha_j)\ne0$. Coefficientwise complex conjugation gives $\overline{Q_x}(T)=\prod_j(1-\overline{z_j}T)$, because conjugation preserves finite sums and products. A coefficient $a+bi$ is fixed by conjugation exactly when $b=0$, so $Q_x\in\mathbf R[T]$ is equivalent to $\overline{Q_x}=Q_x$. Both products have constant coefficient $1$ and degree $n$. By the uniqueness-up-to-reordering clause 3 of [lem-weil-reciprocal-root-factorization], equality of these products implies equality of the multisets $(z_j)$ and $(\overline{z_j})$. Conversely equality of those multisets makes their products equal. This proves precisely the asserted reality equivalence at $x$, hence at every closed point.

source.place: Definition: determinant, inverse eigenvalues, logarithmic weight, reality equivalence and constructible-stalk clause.

proof.text: For each nonzero local eigenvalue $\alpha$, injectivity of the field embedding makes $\iota(\alpha)\ne0$, and [def-weil-complex-absolute-value] gives $|\iota(\alpha)|>0$. Also $q_x=q^{e_x}>1$ in [sk-d-real-setup]. The logarithms are therefore taken on positive inputs and [def-wf-positive-real-logarithm] gives $\log q_x>0$, so the displayed quotient is a well-defined real number. The punctual-purity and upper-weight predicates are exactly the stated universal equality and inequality for this number; no assertion about a mixed filtration is being substituted for the pointwise bound.

proof.text: For a constructible Weil sheaf, use the finite-dimensional stalk and its local geometric-Frobenius automorphism from the stalk-operator convention in [def-weil-punctual-weights]. This citation supplies that local datum only, not its separate mixed-filtration predicate or its stronger choice of coefficient isomorphism. Replace $(V,\rho(F_x))$ by $(\mathcal F_{\bar x},F_x)$ in the definitions. Steps 1 and 3 apply to each such automorphism without a global representation or a rank-constancy hypothesis. Step 4 uses the same residue cardinality and the embedding of this item. A zero stalk gives polynomial $1$ and an empty eigenvalue multiset, so the purity and bound predicates there are vacuous and reality holds. This realizes the final constructible clause without imposing lissity on the whole sheaf.

tool_uses.why: Uses the generic uniqueness of a product of nonzero reciprocal-root factors to identify multiplicities and compare a polynomial with its complex conjugate; no lemma in this unit states this polynomial tool.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q17-3aa67483a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the new node, the unit record and every cited node in full. The statement matches main-20261015 sk-d-real-weights clause by clause, with additions that only fix notation and nothing weakened; the unit has no steps, so realized={statement:[item],steps:[]} is right. Step 1 is correct: charpoly monic of degree n, factorization over Qlb, det F≠0 and det=(-1)^n chi(0) give nonzero alpha_j, reversal of the product gives P_x=prod(1-alpha_j T), and clause 3 of lem-weil-reciprocal-root-factorization (P(0)=1, degree n) gives the multiplicities. Step 2: conjugacy independence holds because the determinant does not depend on the basis. Step 3: reality equivalence via clause 3 over C applied to Q and its conjugate. Step 4: |iota(alpha)|>0 and q_x=q^{e_x}>1, so log q_x>0. Step 5: the stalk and local-operator convention of def-weil-punctual-weights, the same one def-wf-iota-real uses; its iota-isomorphism and mixed-filtration clauses are not used, and the zero-stalk case is handled. Small cases checked: rank 1 with alpha=1 and alpha=q_x, nonreal scalar, conjugate pair, Jordan block, e_x>1. New node def-wf-positive-real-logarithm is an exact Mathlib leaf: Real.log, log_of_pos, exp_log, log_exp and log_pos are at the claimed lines 44/50/59/75/188 of Log/Basic.lean.
